questions.question: Which engine powers BOTH Google Chrome and Node.js?

options.text: SpiderMonkey
V8
Chakra
JavaScriptCore

questions.explanation: V8 is Google's open-source engine used inside Chrome and as the core of Node.js.

questions.question: What is the first stage a JS engine performs after reading source code?

options.text: Execute it line by line immediately
Parse it into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
Compile directly to machine code
Send it to the GPU

questions.explanation: The Parser tokenizes and validates syntax, producing an AST before compilation/execution.

questions.question: JIT stands for Just-In-Time. What does JIT compilation do in V8?

options.text: Interprets code once and discards it
Optimizes frequently-run ('hot') code paths dynamically
Only runs during page load
Disables the garbage collector

questions.explanation: V8 uses Ignition (interpreter) + Turbofan (optimizing compiler) to optimize hot code at runtime.

questions.question: Is Node.js a JavaScript engine?

options.text: Yes, Node.js is the engine
No, Node.js is a runtime that embeds the V8 engine
No, it is a browser
Yes, but only on Windows

questions.explanation: Node.js is a runtime (V8 + libuv + C++ addons). The engine inside it is V8.

questions.question: Which component of the engine reclaims unused memory automatically?

options.text: The Call Stack
The Parser
The Garbage Collector
The Event Loop

questions.explanation: V8's garbage collector (minor/major) reclaims unreachable objects from the heap.

questions.question: What commonly causes V8 to DEOPTIMIZE (revert optimized code to slower code)?

options.text: Using consistent object shapes
Reassigning a variable to a different type in a hot path
Adding 'use strict'
Declaring const variables

questions.explanation: Type changes break inline caches / hidden classes, forcing deoptimization of hot functions.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about the Event Loop?

options.text: It is part of the JavaScript language spec
It is provided by the runtime environment (browser/Node), not the engine itself
It lives inside V8 directly
It only exists in Node.js

questions.explanation: The Event Loop is runtime-provided (libuv in Node, browser APIs). The engine handles execution contexts & call stack.

questions.question: In Angular, what does Zone.js patching help the engine/runtime trigger?

options.text: CSS animations
Change detection after async operations
Garbage collection
HTTP caching

questions.explanation: Zone.js monkey-patches async APIs so Angular knows when to run change detection.
